ac:rich-text-body.p: This page uses four attachments: control-coverage-venn.png, control-coverage-hdf-sources.png, control-coverage-poam-loop.png and control-coverage.csv. publish-confluence.sh uploads them with the page.

p: Each format automates evidence for a different set of controls, and each works without the other. HDF reaches the technical controls through InSpec profiles and scanner mappings. OSCAL reaches the documentary and management controls through its models, including POA&M. Together they produce automated evidence for 166 of the 300 active base controls, with 12 counted by both. OSCAL adds a layer HDF has no equivalent for: it can validate the written claim for every control in the baseline, including the ones no tool can test.

p: HDF's circle is measured: every control that at least one published mapping or InSpec profile tags. OSCAL reaches in three tiers. Its circle holds the controls where an OSCAL document is the evidence, plus physical controls inherited from a leveraged cloud authorization (the dashed subset). The frame is the third tier: every control's written response can be validated automatically, even where the evidence behind it is human.

ac:image.ac:alt: Venn diagram of HDF and OSCAL control coverage

p.em: Counts are Rev 5 base controls; an enhancement tag such as AC-2(1) counts toward AC-2. *SI-1 lands in the overlap because the Docker CIS profile tags it. The inherited subset assumes a system hosted on a FedRAMP-authorized cloud whose authorization provides the PE controls; on-premises, those move outside the circles. Validation proves a claim is complete, consistent and current, not that the control is implemented.

h2: POA&M: automated management, not just a list
p: An OSCAL POA&M risk is a record with a lifecycle: status (open, investigating, remediating, deviation-requested, deviation-approved, closed), a deadline, remediations with milestone tasks, and a risk-log of dated status changes. Fed by HDF results on every run, it tracks RA-5 and SI-2 remediation windows without a spreadsheet. HDF can also manage the same loop alone through Amendments.

ac:image.ac:alt: POA&M remediation loop between HDF and OSCAL

p.em: This loop is why CA-5, RA-5, RA-7 and SI-2 sit in the overlap. HDF detects and re-tests; the POA&M carries deadline, owner, milestones and an auditable status history. HDF Amendments have no permanent entries: every override requires expiresAt.

p: HDF carries the technical families (AC, AU, CM, IA, SC, SI). OSCAL carries CA, PL and the -1 policy control in every family, and PE through inheritance on a cloud-hosted system. PS, PT and most of PM stay with people, with their claims still validated.

ul.li: Universe: the 300 active base controls in NIST's official SP 800-53 Rev 5 OSCAL catalog (24 withdrawn controls excluded).

HDF, mapped (105): the union of NIST IDs in the hdf-mappings tables for AWS Config, ScoutSuite, Nessus, Nikto, Checkov, CWE, OWASP and Hipcheck, plus tag nist on controls in 44 of the 55 MITRE SAF InSpec baselines that could be cloned (11 listed on the SAF site were private or moved). Rev 4 tags count where the base control is still active in Rev 5.
HDF, structural (+3): CA-2 from the Plan document, CA-5 from Amendments of type poam, RA-7 from waivers and risk adjustments. CA-7, CM-8, CA-3 and SR-4 were already mapped.

OSCAL, evidence (49): my classification of where the document itself is the evidence: SSP (PL-2, PL-8 boundary and architecture, RA-2 categorization, CA-9 internal connections), profile (PL-10, PL-11), SAP and SAR (CA-2, CA-7, CA-8 pen testing, CP-4 and IR-3 exercise results), POA&M (CA-5, PM-4, RA-7, and the remediation windows in RA-5 and SI-2), authorization actions (CA-6), interconnections (CA-3), leveraged authorizations (SA-9), inventory (CM-8, PM-5), component definitions (SA-4), and hashed plans in back-matter with review dates (the 20 -1 controls, PL-4, PL-7, CP-2, IR-8, CM-9, SA-5, SR-2).
OSCAL, inherited (21): PE-2 through PE-23, marked inherited with a provided-uuid pointing at what the cloud provider's authorization exports. This holds for cloud-hosted systems only.

OSCAL, validated (300): not counted as coverage. Every baselined control's response can be checked for a matching statement, resolvable component, role and evidence references, allowed ODP values, and unexpired observations.
What a count means: at least one tool can produce evidence tagged to the control. It does not mean every part of the control is satisfied; most mappings cover one part (for example AC-2(j)).
